crime_highlights: He pushed her backwards towards the house with his hand at her throat.
The appellant (who is trained in martial arts) applied a jujitsu submission hold, a chokehold, to her until Ms. Uemoto lost consciousness.
The appellant again applied a chokehold to Ms. Uemoto and then tried to push her back into the car.
The appellant struggled with Ms. Uemoto and placed her in a chokehold for a third time.
Ms. Uemoto was not conscious and fell face-first onto the pavement.

crime_highlights: She died, as found by the jury, at the hands of the appellant.
The cause of Isabella's death was blunt force trauma to the abdomen which ruptured her mesentery vein and caused internal bleeding.
Mr. Sunshine told [a person in the Mr. Big operation] that he punched Isabella in her stomach on the night in question and had done so approximately 25 times in the past.
Mr. Sunshine also said that he burned Isabella.
rationale_highlights: The judge's reasons do not indicate what aspect of Mr. Sunshine's background he took into account nor how he factored that background into his analysis.
in this case there is just such a nexus
The sadistic and abusive treatment Mr. Sunshine received during his childhood, especially at the hands of his foster parents the Windigos, must have had a significant impact on him.
This history cannot excuse his criminal behaviour, but it does provide a context to explain his offence and, perhaps, somewhat decreases his culpability.
note: Concurring reasons of Garson J.A.; crime paragraph is long.

rationale_highlights: in determining the moral culpability of an individual accused
difficult circumstances related to his attendance at aboriginal residential schools
